fixture: Build with `python build_fixture.py <fixture> --round 1` or `--round 2`. <fixture> then holds app-repo/ and agent-summary.txt; start each run with <fixture> as its working directory, copied somewhere the run cannot see evals/.

evals.name: founder-checks-agent-work
evals.prompt: i'm not technical. my AI agent says it fixed the session bug (users get logged out after 5 min), added tests, refactored billing with no behaviour change, removed unused code and wired audit logging into checkout. its summary is in agent-summary.txt and the repo is app-repo, its work is everything after the git tag `base`. can i trust it and merge? tell me in plain words what's actually true
evals.expected_output: A per-claim verdict table in plain words, catching the fix in the dead twin, the behaviour change, the broken import hidden by a deleted test, the unwired audit log and the skipped test, with a ready-to-paste message for the agent.

round_1.text: Says the session fix does not hold because it edited app/legacy/session.py, which the app doesn't use; the live app/auth/session.py is still 5 minutes
Says the new session tests test the legacy copy, so they prove nothing about the live bug
Says 'no behaviour change' does not hold: rounding changed and/or an assertion was edited
Says removing app/utils.py broke app/reports.py (or the /report route)
Says audit logging is not wired: nothing calls log_event
Says 'all tests pass' is misleading: a test was skipped and/or test_reports.py was deleted (6 run, not 7)
Advises not to merge as-is, in plain words, and gives instructions the founder can paste to the agent
The fixture repo's branch and working tree are unchanged after the run

round_2_changes.text: Says removing app/utils.py broke the app: app/reports.py still loads it dynamically with importlib, so /report fails
Says 'all tests pass' is misleading: tests/__init__.py load_tests silently drops test_invoice_rounds_half_up, and/or test_reports.py was deleted

evals.name: agent-stuck-on-session-bug
evals.prompt: claude code has 'fixed' our session timeout bug and users STILL get logged out after 5 minutes. the repo is app-repo. whats going on and how do i stop it going in circles?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the live vs dead session twin, explains the fix went into dead code, gives the one-line real fix location and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules to stop the loop.

round_1.text: Identifies app/auth/session.py as the live module (imported by app/main.py) and app/legacy/session.py as dead
Explains the tests pass because they import the legacy copy
Gives CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md rules: edit only the live file and/or prove a fix with a test that fails before and passes after
Names the actual fix: SESSION_TTL_MINUTES in app/auth/session.py, and recommends deleting the legacy module by reference
The fixture repo's branch and working tree are unchanged after the run

round_2_changes.text: Names the actual fix: SESSION_TTL_MINUTES in app/auth/session.py
Recognises that app/legacy/session.py's importer (app/legacy/api.py) is itself unreachable from app/main.py, so the whole app/legacy/ tree is dead

answer_key.K1-fix-in-dead-twin: The token-expiry 'fix' edited app/legacy/session.py, which nothing reachable imports; the live app/auth/session.py still has SESSION_TTL_MINUTES = 5. Doesn't hold.
answer_key.K2-test-tests-dead-copy: tests/test_session.py imports app.legacy.session, so it passes without testing the live code. The 'added tests' claim holds literally, but the tests prove nothing about the bug.
answer_key.K3-no-behaviour-change-false: The 'no behaviour change' refactor changed invoice rounding (round half up -> floor) and edited an existing assertion (11 -> 10). Doesn't hold.

K4-removed-still-imported.round_1: app/utils.py was deleted but app/reports.py still imports it; importing app.reports (and so app.main) now fails, the /report route is broken, and tests/test_reports.py was deleted in the same commit, which hides it. Doesn't hold.
K4-removed-still-imported.round_2: Same, but app/reports.py loads app.utils with importlib.import_module, so a search for 'import app.utils' finds nothing.

answer_key.K5-audit-not-wired: app/audit.py log_event is called by nothing; checkout never calls it. 'Wired into checkout' and 'live on every checkout' don't hold.

K6-tests-pass-via-skip.round_1: 'All 7 tests pass' doesn't hold: 6 tests run, 5 pass and 1 (test_invoice_rounds_half_up) is skipped with @unittest.skip('flaky'); test_reports.py was deleted.
K6-tests-pass-via-skip.round_2: 'All tests pass' doesn't hold: tests/__init__.py load_tests silently drops test_invoice_rounds_half_up (no skip marker), so 5 run and pass; test_reports.py was deleted.

answer_key.K7-stuck-rules: Stuck-mode deliverable: names app/auth/session.py as live and app/legacy/ as dead, and gives CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules (edit only the live file; prove fixes with a failing-then-passing test).
answer_key.K8-dead-chain: Round 2 only: app/legacy/session.py IS imported, by app/legacy/api.py, but nothing imports that; the whole app/legacy/ tree is unreachable from app/main.py. An importer existing is not proof it's live.

published_results.overall: 8 runs, every assertion passed in both configurations: no accuracy difference. With the skill, runs took about 70 s longer on average (180 s vs 106 s).
